comments.value:
Vrchat is a multiplayer environment and has a dedicated streamer community, they're everywhere 

The solution to avoid streamers is to avoid public worlds but at the same time, a majority of streamers also stay in friend/invite only sessions. They also almost-always have block avatars by default, because they don't know you either

But that's not the real danger, the fact that people will know that they're streaming will paint a huge target on streamers, and toxic people love to harass streamers.
By using the Icon, it would be treated as a "badge of shame" on streamers with people getting immediately mad at them and spread the mindset that "it's a streamer, eugh" or "there's a streamer here, guys lets leave", or like when ever you see an account with a twitch url. A lot of streamers are good people and dedicate their times to exploring VRchat and meeting its amazing people, they're still people who want to play the game just like you and I don't think they should target themselves to do that.

If you're worried about looking bad on a stream or anything, it's the internet, as long as you're not a dick, it'll be fine

@{5a570cf1b301553d0104bddd|full_name}: If someone is streaming they are already marked as a streamer because they are streaming live to a platform like twitch which anyone ingame can go and check. Their actions are already affected because they have to be mindful of the TOS on their streaming platform of choice as well. Players target streamers regardless of how they find out. That is a separate issue.

Tails as an example is a long time VRC streamer who has always had a marker on their avatar that they are streaming ingame and I've never seen that affect their viewercount or streaming experience.

What's more important here is that people are somehow told that they are live on camera. VRC has become a very very social game and it's unfair on those to constantly have to concerned that someone they don't know could be streaming their activities and so they don't have to ask every new person they meet "are you streaming". This saves both parties involved time and effort.

This feature doesn't have to be enforced either. It just has to be there and ready to use so a streamer new to VRchat can simply turn it on in the settings menu rather then spending time adding it to their avatar and all the other annoyances that come along with that.
@{5b52ba672b29a515be8ff219|full_name}: Almost all screen recording is done by third-party software but there are ways for software to detect that it is being recorded by something.

@{5b655caa6018440ebf481033|full_name}: this is intrusive on peoples systems, being a public space people should be considerate and curtious with each other. That being said its a public space. Private worlds exist <3

@{5a1a3264c945276834dd45df|full_name}: Discord as an example detects if you have streaming software running and enables the streaming mode in your settings accordingly. Most methods would be non intrusive to your computer.
@{5b655caa6018440ebf481033|full_name}: but that can be disabled. What you are asking for suggests otherwise.

This post is not an indication of work or favoring for/against a feature like this, but just feedback. Additionally, keep in mind I am not a software engineer!

The only way for us to detect if someone is recording the screen is to analyze the process list on someone's computer. This is invasive and difficult to do without appearing (to malware scanners like Windows Defender) like a malicious piece of software. It is also absurdly complex, and a variation of this technique is used in anti-cheat software that entire companies are dedicated to developing.

In short, this is a good suggestion, but likely exceedingly difficult to execute.

@{5acad9ecc9dba010c9c3ec68|full_name}: simple solution, rather then making it the idea of if they are streaming force an icon to show they are, instead create a simple toggle in the menu to indicate you are streaming. I've seen several streamers already post a live icon above them, so I'm sure several would use that feature as a friendly of saying "hey I'm streaming"
I guess a lot of people would use it optionally, like on Discord, but I agree with you, and I also have very mixed feelings about being recorded.
I don't see why being recorded should matter that much.
And have everyone in the instance walk up to streamers and yell out racist stuff. SeemsGood

details: Not everyone wants to be recorded in VRChat for many reasons, there should be a feature that allows streamers to mark if they are currently recording, or later on in development, force an icon above the player that shows they are recording or streaming. Players have the right to know if they are being recorded in a public space. Also a nice feature would be to automatically become muted or have your avatar become invisible to a player marked as recording.
title: Mark players recording VRC
